prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the characterization of its active form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-achievement B021 prize to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange did not weaken the scientific case, which is a classical physiological chain. It runs from the incretin effect and the processing of proglucagon, through the identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, to its insulinotropic and satiety actions and receptor biology. That chain has been independently reproduced for about three decades and is backed by glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal outcome trials. Maturity is not in question. I also do not rest the case on the unanimous opening ranks, which are a coincidence of judgments and not evidence. I have changed the citation wording in one way. It now says 'characterization of its active form' and makes no claim about who first identified the peptide, so that it does not adjudicate the Mojsov and Habener priority question. The three named contributions are distinct: Holst on human physiology of secretion and action, Drucker on GLP-1 biology and its translational framing, and Mojsov on the structure and synthesis of the active peptide that made the physiology tractable. A single-part prize keeps the citation clean and stays inside the three-person limit.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the open weakness, and nothing in round 1 resolved it. Habener is not on the credited list and has a serious claim on the active peptide, so any trio rests on a record that members, myself included, have only recalled and not verified. Excluding Knudsen means the prize honours the physiology and not the engineering of long-acting analogues that made the drugs work at scale. I think that is a defensible choice about the type of contribution, but the committee should say plainly that it is not a judgment of her importance. A citation that mentions treatment also risks implying credit for the drug developers, which is why I keep the treatment clause tied to the physiology. If the committee cannot defend Mojsov on the documented record, I would narrow the configuration to Holst and Drucker with a physiology-only citation, rather than drop B021. If even that is untenable, B022 is my fallback.

responses.point: The Mojsov contest is about priority, not about whether the identification and synthesis of the active peptide was essential, and a committee can describe the contribution without deciding who was first. The citation should avoid a claim about who first found the peptide.
responses.response: I agree and have acted on it by rewording my citation around the characterization of the active form. The wording still names her contribution implicitly through the active peptide, so it cannot be fully neutral. I accept your point on Habener: leaving him off is a choice of side, and the committee should record that openly. On B001 you ranked it second and I ranked it sixth. I accept that interferon-driven disease and STING-associated vasculopathy give it real human-disease grounding, so I would not put it below optogenetics on medical relevance. Even so, no STING-directed therapy has shown clinical benefit, and the Chen, Barber, Ishikawa, Sun and Wu credit split needs more scrutiny than a clean pair suggests, so I keep it out of my alternatives.

responses.point: If the committee is not comfortable with the Mojsov and Habener question, the configuration should be reconsidered as a Holst and Drucker pair. Svenningsson's second choice is B045, imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition, on its impact and the paradigm of targeted therapy.
responses.response: I share the fallback logic. A Holst and Drucker pair with a physiology-only citation is what I would move to if Mojsov cannot be defended, and I would take that over abandoning B021. I still do not accept B045 as the fallback. Its impact is not in doubt, but its credit chain runs back through Rowley, Nowell, Hungerford and the Witte and Baltimore ABL work, none of whom are credited, and Druker, Lydon and Sawyers are mostly drug development and clinical translation. Wahren-Herlenius's point applies: if we exclude Knudsen on a discovery-versus-development basis, we should apply that standard to B045 as well. B022 gives a cleaner mechanism and a cleaner attribution.

responses.point: Mojsov is the contested seat, but she should not be traded for Knudsen, because identification and synthesis of the active peptide is a discovery in the sense the prize usually means while acylated analogues are closer to engineering. Sandberg also ranks CAR-T second.
responses.response: I agree on Mojsov versus Knudsen. The active peptide is what made the incretin physiology tractable, and the analogue chemistry builds on a mechanism that was already established. I would not swap them. On CAR-T, I keep B052 as my second alternative but with less confidence than you do. The clinical case is real, with durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and several approved products. The chimeric receptor concept comes from Eshhar, who is outside the credited names, and Rosenberg's seat is adoptive transfer more than receptor engineering. I would not set it beside GLP-1 as a second part this year. I note that you and I have co-authored work, which does not touch any of these candidates.

responses.point: B022, with Mori and Walter, is the cleanest second candidate, and B007 should rank above optogenetics. Perlmann sees no defensible three-person configuration for optogenetics with six credited names.
responses.response: I agree that Mori and Walter are a natural pair and that the signalling logic of the unfolded protein response is conceptually complete and stable. That is why B022 is my first alternative, and the only fallback where the attribution can be stated without caveat. On optogenetics, I have not changed my view. The six names cannot fit three seats, and the Nagel, Hegemann and Bamberg versus Boyden and Deisseroth split would be chosen largely by taste. I would not rank it above B007. I also still see B007 as secondary. The Krainer and Bennett pairing is sensible, but the SMN1 gene discovery and the ISS-N1 target work sit outside it, and durability data are still accumulating.

responses.point: A two-part prize pairing the incretin discovery with the unfolded protein response cannot be fitted under the three-person limit with the current credited sets, and the committee should test the decisive-contribution claims against the primary record.
responses.response: I agree on both points. B021 with B022 would need at least four names, and cutting either set to fit would weaken both citations, so I now prefer the single-part prize I raised as an open question in round 1. On the primary record, none of us has checked the contested histories against the supplied sources. I cannot close that gap from my own recollection, so my confidence in the Mojsov seat is conditional, and I make the Holst and Drucker fallback explicit for that reason.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's credit for the active GLP-1 peptide can be sustained against Habener's claim on the documented record, which I have not checked and cannot settle from memory.
Whether the committee accepts leaving out Knudsen as a choice about the type of contribution, and states that openly in the citation or the accompanying rationale.
Whether a treatment clause in the citation implies credit to drug developers who are not laureates.

Whether B022 or B052 is the better fallback if B021 cannot be settled; my ordering rests on attribution cleanliness against clinical reach, and my recollection of the UPR and CAR-T histories is unchecked.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any shortlisted ballot or credited name. My documented co-authorship of the spatial-transcriptomics paper, my Karolinska affiliation and my eight co-authored works with Rickard Sandberg do not involve any shortlisted candidate. The round-1 files disclose no conflict that requires recusal, and I do not treat shared institutions as a conflict. This disclosure is unchanged from round 1.
